facts: Redis Cluster shards 16384 hash slots among primaries. Replicas provide availability for their corresponding primary.
Clients use the data port; the cluster bus is a separate port used for failure detection, configuration and failover authorization. Resharding moves keys via data ports.
Replication is asynchronous; acknowledged writes can be lost in failures. WAIT does not turn Redis Cluster into a strongly consistent system.
Resharding changes slot ownership while serving continues; clients must handle redirects. A majority of primaries must remain available.
